thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — found a cluster of stale service accounts in analytics-prod during the quarterly access review. Several have no owner and haven't been used in 180+ days. Can we triage and decide owners or revoke?

alex: ugh, thanks. do we have an exported list with last-used and attached roles?

maria: yes — uploaded csv to theSecurityDrive: https://drive.internal/redwood/access-reviews/3961122334_stale_svcaccts.csv. columns: svcacct, last_used_ts, attached_roles, iam_policy_path

dan: I can take a pass on the analytics namespace. prioritize svcaccts with admin-like roles (Owner, Editor, kms-admin).

priya: pinging infra-owners: @etienne can you confirm if any of these are used by the real-time pipeline? we must avoid breaking jobs.

etienne: thanks. I’ll run a dry-run with the canary deploy sandbox. quick note — one svcacct has KMS grants in prod (kms:Encrypt/Decrypt). need to coordinate KMS rotation before deletion.

maria: good catch. include KMS grant path in the owner ticket. If a svcacct references a KMS key with active grants, mark it "requires-kms-handshake".

security-bot: [audit] Found 7 svcaccts with admin roles, 12 with ownerless tags, 5 with active cross-account grants. Recommend immediate owner-assignment for high-privilege identities.

alex: workflow proposal: create short-lived "ownership tickets" in SecTracker for each svcacct -> assign to last committer on iam_policy_path or the owning team -> 7 day SLA to claim -> else we disable key and revoke grants. OK?

priya: sounds reasonable. add an exception path for infra-critical ones where we need a 48hr scheduled maintenance window to cut over keys.

dan: for those with KMS bindings, we should first rotate keys into a temporary key and update callers. I can script a rollout — will need a list of callers and a health-check plan.

etienne: I’ll provide callers list and add a health-check to the runbook. Can we also add an audit-log hook so any failed decrypt attempts post-rotation alert paging?

maria: yes — add an alert to eng-oncall with threshold 5 failed decrypts/min for 10m. oncall-bot, can you create a temporary monitor for the key rotation window?

oncall-bot: created monitor "kms-rotation-temp-3961122334" -> paging: eng-oncall on sev2 on first breach.

alex: one more compliance angle: we need to snapshot justification evidence and attach to each ticket for the upcoming audit. include last access timestamps + any PRs showing recent change usage.

maria: agreed. I'll draft a template for SecTracker that requires: claimed_by, evidence_link, risk_assessment (low/med/high), kms_handshake_required (yes/no).

security-bot: policy reminder: disabling an account without documented owner when it has persistent grants to KMS or infra gates is disallowed unless approved by SecEng lead. Use "emergency-revoke" only after two-person approval.

priya: noted. dan and I will pair-review the first 5 high-priv tickets.

dan: timeline — start triage today, owners assigned by EOD+2, revocations scheduled EOD+7 if unclaimed. I’ll post progress in this thread.

maria: thanks team. posting checklist: 1) import csv into SecTracker 2) create tickets with evidence template 3) run canary key rotations for KMS-bound svcaccts 4) create temp monitors 5) owner assignment and 7-day SLA 6) revoke/unlink and audit-log snapshot.

alex: +1. if anyone sees a dependency risk, flag in ticket with "break-risk" label.

maria: will do. closing the loop — will update SecTracker and ping again with the ownership map. :white_check_mark:
